thread:
sam_newhire: hey team, day 1 weirdness. i'm at a coworking spot and after connecting wg my browser keeps getting a login/captive page instead of our internal docs (docs.internal.redwood). i can ssh to bastion fine, wg says it's up, but browsing internal services hits the coworking portal. anyone seen this? :slightly_frowning_face:

wg-bot: WireGuard: peer=sam_newhire, latest_handshake=18s ago, endpoint=198.51.100.99:51820, allowedips=10.0.0.0/8

izzy-eng: welcome! yep, lots of public wifi/coworking networks run captive portals that intercept DNS/HTTP until you auth. sometimes they also block or NAT UDP so even if wg shows a handshake some traffic leaks to the portal. quick check: can you `curl -v --resolve "docs.internal.redwood:443:10.10.2.5" https://docs.internal.redwood/` from your laptop?

sam_newhire: curl with --resolve gives cert mismatch (expected CN docs.internal.redwood, got captive.local) and hangs otherwise. traceroute to 10.10.2.5 stops at 100.64.0.1.

morton-sre: 100.64.0.1 = CGNAT from the ISP/captive network. captive portals often do DNS hijack so internal hostnames resolve to the portal's webserver. two easy workarounds: 1) if you're okay doing interactive auth, open a plain http site (http://neverssl.com) to trigger the portal login, authenticate, then WireGuard may start routing properly; OR 2) bypass the coworking network entirely for internal traffic by using sshuttle: `sshuttle -r sam@bastion.redwood.internal 10.0.0.0/8 --dns` which forwards IP+DNS over SSH without fiddly per-port tunnels.

sam_newhire: tried neverssl, got the portal, logged in, but the portal still hijacks DNS and my browser resolves docs.internal.redwood to the portal IP. after login curl to internal ip still timed out.

izzy-eng: in that case sshuttle is nice because it doesn't require root on the bastion and handles DNS. command: `sshuttle -r sam@bastion.redwood.internal 10.0.0.0/8 --dns -x 0.0.0.0/0` (the -x keeps all other traffic local). once running, open https://docs.internal.redwood and it should go through the bastion. note: sshuttle internally uses python and iptables, it will ask for your sudo password locally.

kali-security: short policy note: using sshuttle or an SSH SOCKS proxy for onboarding is acceptable. do not request expanding allowlists to include consumer/coworking IP ranges. also avoid leaving long-lived tunnels open on untrusted networks. please close sshuttle when you're done and mark the session in the onboarding checklist.

morton-sre: if sshuttle isn't available, fallback: `ssh -D 1080 sam@bastion.redwood.internal -N` and set browser to socks5h://localhost:1080. that also fixes DNS leakage if you use socks5h.

sam_newhire: sshuttle worked! docs load and I could complete SSO. thanks so much 🙏. i'll close the tunnel when i'm finished.

izzy-eng: added a short entry to the new-hires network doc with both sshuttle and ssh -D recipes and a note about captive portals.

doc-bot: created NET-912: "onboarding: captive-portal + sshuttle + socks proxy snippets" (created by izzy-eng).
